entries.reason: iOS 10 generates the pair and answers the private key; iOS 6 generates the same pair with SecKeyGeneratePair, which it has had since iOS 2, and honours kSecAttrIsPermanent the same way
entries.effect: the release's own generator is asked with the parameters as they were given, the public half is released and the private key answered; a refusal comes back as NULL and a CFError of domain NSOSStatusErrorDomain carrying the release's OSStatus, never as a crash
entries.source: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, where Security exports _SecKeyGeneratePair and none of the iOS 10 names; the host's own Security for the shape of the CFError

entries.reason: iOS 6 has the two private entry points this is made of: SecKeyCopyPublicBytes serialises the public half of any key, and SecKeyCreateFromPublicData makes a key of it, dividing RSA from EC by the algorithm identifier
entries.effect: the public key of a key pair or a private key, and NULL where the release cannot serialise one, which is what the header says the function answers when no public key is available
entries.source: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, where _SecKeyCopyPublicBytes is at 0x32e90511, _SecKeyCreateFromPublicData at 0x32e90545 and _SecKeyGetAlgorithmID at 0x32e904fd, all three disassembled; the same three are exported by every cache from 6.0 to 10.3.4

entries.reason: the algorithm of iOS 10 is the padding of iOS 6's SecKeyEncrypt for the three the release can do, and nothing else is claimed
entries.effect: RSAEncryptionRaw, RSAEncryptionPKCS1 and RSAEncryptionOAEPSHA1 are the release's kSecPaddingNone, kSecPaddingPKCS1 and kSecPaddingOAEP; every other algorithm is refused with NULL and a CFError that names the algorithm and the key, as the system refuses an algorithm a key cannot do, and a refusal by the release is its own OSStatus in a CFError
entries.source: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, where Security exports _SecKeyEncrypt and _SecKeyGetBlockSize; SecKey.h of SDK 16.4 for the padding values and the algorithm names; the host's own Security for the shape of the CFError and of its message

entries.reason: the mirror of the encryption, over the release's own SecKeyDecrypt
entries.effect: the same three algorithms over kSecPaddingNone, kSecPaddingPKCS1 and kSecPaddingOAEP, the answer cut to the length the release wrote; every other algorithm and every refusal by the release come back as NULL and a CFError
entries.source: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, where Security exports _SecKeyDecrypt and _SecKeyGetBlockSize; SecKey.h of SDK 16.4 for the padding values and the algorithm names

entries.reason: iOS 10 answers the PKCS#1 representation of the key it is given; iOS 6 keeps the same bytes, the public ones through SecKeyCopyPublicBytes and whatever the key's own attribute dictionary holds
entries.effect: the private key's PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey where the release's attribute dictionary really holds one, which the port parses before it trusts it, and the PKCS#1 RSAPublicKey where the key is proven to be a public one; where the release holds neither the answer is NULL and a CFError, never the public half in place of a private key
entries.source: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, where _SecKeyCopyPublicBytes and _SecKeyCopyAttributeDictionary are exported; the host's own Security, which answers 270 bytes of PKCS#1 RSAPublicKey for the public half of a 2048-bit key and 1193 bytes of PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey for the private one
